summaries.sde3-backend: Software Development Engineer III (Backend) with 3.5+ years of experience and expertise in TypeScript/Node.js, RESTful APIs and microservices, distributed systems, and scalable backend architecture. Led the AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 to v3 migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services in production Node.js Lambdas at Turbot HQ, cutting policy-code duplication ~60% while keeping systems supported past AWS SDK v2 end-of-life.

work.name: Turbot HQ, Inc.
highlights: Led the AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 to v3 migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services (SecurityHub, CloudWatch, ControlTower, Shield, Comprehend, Pinpoint, RAM, X-Ray, EC2, EFS) in production Node.js Lambdas; reduced policy-code duplication ~60% via templating, keeping the platform supported past AWS SDK v2 EOL.

Built a Kafka-based, event-driven distributed pipeline where consumers asynchronously processed policy-enforcement events; added a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for reliable failure handling and reprocessing.

Designed and developed an internal REST API microservice in Go using the Gin framework as part of a greenfield build of Turbot Guardrails, a high-scale SaaS platform; secured endpoints with OAuth 2.0 authentication via Auth0, containerized with Docker, deployed to AWS EC2, and served as a gRPC client for several internal distributed microservices.

Optimized complex PostgreSQL queries powering customer compliance audits — rewriting AWS IAM policy-evaluation queries with jsonb array elements and multi-stage CTEs — improving query performance 40% and eliminating a class of false-positive findings.

Engineered core features for Tailpipe, a CLI on DuckDB + Parquet, lifting log-processing throughput 30% to 1,000+ logs per second by chunking and batching file reads and streaming writes; reduced memory use to eliminate out-of-memory failures at scale.
Resolved a production incident by diagnosing a Go service stuck in a Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff — investigating pod logs and status and collaborating with the platform team to restore service.
